backyard-landscaping.q: How much does backyard landscaping cost in Australia?
backyard-landscaping.a: Backyard landscaping in Australia typically costs $50 to $150 per square metre, depending on turf, garden beds, and hardscaping involved. A modest backyard makeover might use Sir Walter buffalo turf at around $18 per square metre, garden soil, and mulch, while retaining walls and paving push jobs toward the top of that range. Get a few quotes to compare scope.

backyard-landscaping.q: How long does backyard landscaping take?
backyard-landscaping.a: Most backyard landscaping projects take one to two weeks from clearing to planting, though larger jobs with retaining walls, irrigation, or extensive paving can stretch to four weeks or more. Weather, soil conditions, and how much of the yard needs regrading all affect the timeline, so ask your landscaper for a realistic schedule before work starts.

backyard-landscaping.q: What's included in a backyard landscaping quote?
backyard-landscaping.a: A typical backyard landscaping quote covers site preparation, turf or garden bed installation, soil and mulch, and any retaining walls or edging in the design. Materials like turf run about $18 per square metre and mulch around $15 per 60-litre bag, with labour making up the rest. Always ask for a written, itemised quote before work begins.

burst-pipe-repair.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Australia?
burst-pipe-repair.a: Burst pipe repair in Australia typically costs $80 to $200 per hour, with most straightforward jobs taking one to two hours once the plumber has isolated the water. Replacement pipe adds $6 to $23 per 5-metre length for PEX or around $10 to $16 per metre for copper. Emergency after-hours callouts usually cost more.

burst-pipe-repair.q: Is a burst pipe covered by home insurance?
burst-pipe-repair.a: Most Australian home insurance policies cover sudden, accidental burst pipe damage such as water damage to floors or walls, though the repair of the pipe itself is sometimes excluded. Gradual leaks or wear-related failures are often not covered. Check your policy's product disclosure statement and contact your insurer promptly after a burst pipe.

burst-pipe-repair.q: How quickly should a burst pipe be repaired?
burst-pipe-repair.a: A burst pipe needs urgent attention, ideally within hours, because even a small leak can release a large volume of water quickly and cause serious damage. Shut off the mains water supply immediately, then call an emergency plumber. Acting fast limits damage to floors, walls, and belongings and keeps the eventual repair bill smaller.

concrete-paver-installation.q: How much does concrete paver installation cost in Australia?
concrete-paver-installation.a: Concrete paver installation in Australia typically costs $50 to $150 per square metre, including base preparation, sand bedding, and laying. Bedding sand and crusher dust each add roughly $10 to $21 per bag on top of the paver cost. Patterned laying, cutting around edges, and difficult site access can push a job toward the higher end of that range.

concrete-paver-installation.q: How long do concrete pavers last?
concrete-paver-installation.a: Well-installed concrete pavers typically last 25 to 50 years with basic maintenance such as resealing every few years and keeping joints topped up with sand. Lifespan depends on the base preparation, paver quality, and how much foot or vehicle traffic the area gets. Cracking is usually a sign of poor base compaction rather than the pavers themselves.

concrete-paver-installation.q: Can concrete pavers be laid over an existing concrete slab?
concrete-paver-installation.a: Concrete pavers can often be laid directly over an existing slab if it is sound, level, and draining properly, using a thin mortar bed or paver adhesive instead of a full sand base. Cracked, uneven, or poorly drained slabs usually need repair first. A paving contractor can check the slab's condition before quoting the job.

driveway-paving.q: How much does driveway paving cost in Australia?
driveway-paving.a: Driveway paving in Australia typically costs $50 to $150 per square metre, covering excavation, base preparation, and paver laying. Pavers themselves add roughly $11 per bag of crusher dust and $11 to $21 per bag of bedding sand on top of paver supply. A standard double driveway usually needs 40 to 60 square metres of paving.

driveway-paving.q: How long does driveway paving take?
driveway-paving.a: Most residential driveway paving jobs take two to five days, depending on the driveway's size, whether old concrete needs removing, and how much excavation and base work is required. Weather and access for machinery also affect the schedule. A paver should give a clear day-by-day timeline as part of the quote.

driveway-paving.q: What is the best material for a driveway in Australia?
driveway-paving.a: Concrete pavers, brick pavers, and poured concrete are the most common Australian driveway materials, each with different upkeep and looks. Pavers are easy to repair individually and resist cracking from ground movement, while poured concrete gives a seamless surface but shows cracks over time. Climate, soil type, and budget usually decide the best fit.

floor-tiling.q: How much does floor tiling cost in Australia?
floor-tiling.a: Floor tiling in Australia typically costs $45 to $120 per square metre installed, covering tile adhesive, grout, and labour. Porcelain floor tiles themselves typically run from about $29 to $85 per square metre before installation, so tile choice makes a big difference to the total. Levelling an uneven subfloor first adds further cost.

floor-tiling.q: How long does floor tiling take to dry?
floor-tiling.a: Tile adhesive typically needs 24 to 48 hours to cure enough to walk on, though full grouting usually waits at least 24 hours after tiling. The whole floor should be left to cure fully, often around seven days, before it takes heavy furniture or appliances. Humidity and tile size can extend these times.

floor-tiling.q: Can you tile over an existing floor?
floor-tiling.a: Tiling over an existing floor is often possible if the surface is flat, stable, and well bonded, using the right primer or adhesive for the substrate. Cracked tiles, timber floors that flex, or floors with loose sections usually need preparation or removal first. A tiler can assess the existing floor before quoting.

gyprock-repair.q: How much does gyprock repair cost in Australia?
gyprock-repair.a: Gyprock repair in Australia typically costs $45 to $90 per hour, and a small hole or crack usually takes one to three hours to patch, sand, and paint-ready finish, for a total around $100 to $300. Full sheet replacement costs more once a new $28 to $97 plasterboard sheet, jointing compound, and tape are added to the labour.

gyprock-repair.q: Is Gyprock the same as plasterboard?
gyprock-repair.a: Gyprock is a well-known brand name for plasterboard in Australia, and the two terms are often used interchangeably. Other manufacturers make their own plasterboard products under different brand names, but they perform the same job of lining internal walls and ceilings with a gypsum core between paper facings. All are repaired the same way.

Modern Gyprock plasterboard, made from gypsum and paper, contains no asbestos. Older homes can still have asbestos-containing wall sheeting that looks similar from the surface, so if you are unsure about a wall in an older property, have a sample tested before cutting, sanding, or drilling into it. A licensed tradesperson can arrange testing.

kitchen-sink-installation.q: How much does kitchen sink installation cost in Australia?
kitchen-sink-installation.a: Installing a kitchen sink in Australia typically costs $250 to $600 in labour for a straightforward swap using the existing plumbing, or $600 to $1,600 supply-and-installed for a new sink and mixer tap. Sinks retail from about $170 to $770 and mixer taps from $79 to $477, so fixture choice drives most of the total.

kitchen-sink-installation.q: Can I install a kitchen sink myself?
kitchen-sink-installation.a: Installing a kitchen sink yourself is possible for a straight swap if the new sink matches the existing cutout and plumbing connections. Anything involving new pipework, moving connections, or gas and water compliance is safer left to a licensed plumber, and getting it professionally installed also protects your home insurance and any product warranty.

kitchen-sink-installation.q: What size kitchen sink do I need?
kitchen-sink-installation.a: Kitchen sink sizing depends on your cabinet width and how you use the kitchen, with a single bowl suiting compact kitchens and a double bowl, priced from around $170 to $770, giving more room for washing and prep. Standard base cabinets are usually 600mm or 900mm wide, which limits the sink dimensions that will fit.

mosaic-tiling.q: How much does mosaic tiling cost in Australia?
mosaic-tiling.a: Mosaic tiling in Australia typically costs $45 to $120 per square metre installed, reflecting the extra time needed to lay small tiles precisely. Mosaic sheets themselves cost around $9 to $26 each, with tile adhesive and grout adding a further $27 to $94 combined. Intricate feature areas like splashbacks usually sit toward the top of the range.

mosaic-tiling.q: Where is mosaic tiling used in the home?
mosaic-tiling.a: Mosaic tiling is most popular for kitchen splashbacks, bathroom feature walls, and shower niches, where its small format handles curves and detail better than large tiles. It also works well on pool surrounds and outdoor feature strips because the extra grout lines add slip resistance. Many homeowners use it to highlight a single accent area.

mosaic-tiling.q: Is mosaic tiling hard to install?
mosaic-tiling.a: Mosaic tiling takes more time and patience than standard tiles because each small piece needs even spacing and pressure, but mesh-backed sheets make the process more manageable than loose individual pieces. Getting a level base and consistent grout lines is the trickiest part, so many homeowners still prefer to hire a qualified tiler.

reflective-foil-insulation.q: How much does reflective foil insulation cost in Australia?
reflective-foil-insulation.a: Reflective foil insulation installed in Australia typically costs $10 to $25 per square metre, similar to other insulation types. Material costs are a modest part of that figure since a single roll runs a few hundred dollars, so most of the price covers a professional correctly stapling, lapping, and taping the foil for it to perform properly.

reflective-foil-insulation.q: Does reflective foil insulation work in Australian climates?
reflective-foil-insulation.a: Reflective foil insulation works well in Australia because it reflects radiant heat, which is the main way heat moves through a roof space in hot climates, keeping the home cooler in summer. It performs best with an air gap on the reflective side and is often paired with bulk insulation for winter warmth too.

reflective-foil-insulation.q: Where is reflective foil insulation installed?
reflective-foil-insulation.a: Reflective foil insulation is most commonly installed under roof sheeting or rafters, facing down into the roof space, to block radiant heat before it reaches the ceiling. It can also line external walls during construction. It only works properly with a clear air gap left on the reflective side, so tight-packed installs lose most of the benefit.

roof-restoration.q: How much does roof restoration cost in Australia?
roof-restoration.a: Roof restoration in Australia typically costs $50 to $100 per hour for trade labour, and a full single-storey job usually runs into the thousands once several days of cleaning, priming, membrane coating, and repointing are included. Roof membrane costs around $249 per 15 litres and flexible pointing about $40 per 10 litres, with multiple batches needed for an average roof.

roof-restoration.q: How long does roof restoration take?
roof-restoration.a: A typical single-storey roof restoration takes two to five days, covering pressure cleaning, repairs, priming, and two coats of protective membrane with drying time between coats. Larger or steeper roofs, or those needing more repointing and ridge capping work, can take longer. Wet weather often delays the membrane coating stages specifically.

Roof restoration typically includes high-pressure cleaning, replacing broken or cracked tiles, repointing ridge capping with flexible pointing compound, priming, and applying two coats of protective membrane. It restores the look and waterproofing of an ageing roof without the cost of a full replacement, and usually comes with a workmanship warranty from the roofer.

steel-stud-framing.q: How much does steel stud framing cost in Australia?
steel-stud-framing.a: Steel stud framing in Australia typically costs $45 to $90 per hour for a licensed installer, since it is usually charged as part of a plastering or partition wall job rather than priced separately. A 64mm steel stud costs around $9 to $15 per 3-metre length, so a standard internal wall needs a modest material spend before labour.

steel-stud-framing.q: Is steel stud framing better than timber framing?
steel-stud-framing.a: Steel stud framing resists termites, warping, and shrinkage better than timber, and stays straighter over time, which suits bathrooms, commercial fit-outs, and tall partition walls. Timber framing is often cheaper, easier for tradespeople to modify on site, and remains the standard choice for most Australian house framing. The best option depends on the application.

steel-stud-framing.q: Can steel stud framing be used in load-bearing walls?
steel-stud-framing.a: Standard light-gauge steel studs are designed for non-load-bearing internal partitions, not structural load-bearing walls. Heavier structural steel framing systems can carry loads, but they need engineering design and different stud sizes and thicknesses than the 64mm studs used for typical internal walls. Always confirm the wall's structural role with your builder first.

vanity-installation.q: How much does vanity installation cost in Australia?
vanity-installation.a: Installing a new bathroom vanity in Australia typically costs $800 to $2,500 supply-and-installed, covering the vanity unit, tap, and a plumber's labour to disconnect and reconnect water and waste. Vanities themselves range from about $612 to $1,590 depending on size and finish, with mixer taps adding $93 to $326 on top.

vanity-installation.q: How deep is a vanity in Australia?
vanity-installation.a: Standard bathroom vanities in Australia are usually around 460mm to 465mm deep to fit comfortably in a typical bathroom without crowding the walkway. Slimline vanities as shallow as 350mm are available for tight ensuites, while some wall-hung and freestanding styles run deeper for extra storage. Always measure your space before ordering one.

vanity-installation.q: Can I install a bathroom vanity myself?
vanity-installation.a: Fitting a vanity cabinet in place is a manageable DIY task for a confident homeowner, but connecting the tap and waste to the water supply and drain should be left to a licensed plumber. Getting the plumbing done professionally protects your warranty and avoids leaks that can damage flooring and cabinetry over time.
